Independent finite reconstruction for n=3 through 7 from the defining edges and recomputed degrees
correctness.rationale: Deleting a₀ leaves b₀ and all aᵢ at degree n−1 and all other bⱼ at degree n−2. If b₀ is not selected, no selected B-neighbor can strongly dominate a missing aᵢ, so all of A′ is selected; that suffices, since n−1≥2 and a remaining bⱼ misses at most one member of A′. With b₀ selected, every missing aᵢ is covered, and respectively zero, one, or at least two selected aᵢ force all bⱼ, just the matching-index bᵢ, or none of the other B-vertices. The four disjoint contributions give the polynomial coefficientwise. At n=3 only A′ is minimum; for n≥4 the minimum is three, with (n−1)+C(n−1,2)+[n=4] possibilities. Substitution at z=1 gives the stated total. Direct independent enumeration over the residual adjacency and degree condition for n=3,…,7 matched every coefficient; for example n=4 gave (0,0,0,7,20,18,7,1) and the five totals were 13,53,225,945,3905.
residual_risks: The case-1 phrase about all neighbors should be read as all selected candidate neighbors, since b₀ is an unselected neighbor. This does not change the proof.
The supplied verifier uses int.bit_count(), so its recorded Python 3.8 compatibility is inaccurate; use Python 3.10 or later. The bounded independent reproduction does not replace the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The crown is a natural matching-deleted complete bipartite family, and vertex deletion produces one high-degree B-vertex and asymmetric domination constraints. An exact all-cardinality polynomial answers more than scalar sensitivity, including the n=3 and n=4 boundary effects, the shapes and exact counts of minimum sets, and total-set counts. The elementary proof does not make the finer enumerator a substitution into a prior result.
residual_risks: Value is for one vertex deletion in this family with residual degrees; no multi-deletion or generic enumerator is claimed.
